\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]\draw[{Stealth}-{Stealth}] (-0.6,0)--(5.6,0);\foreach \x in {0,1,2,3,4,5} {\draw (\x,0)--(\x,-0.12); \node[below] at (\x,-0.14) {$\x$};}\fill (0,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (0,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,1.26) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,1.26) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,1.58) circle (2.2pt);\fill (5,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\node[below] at (2.5,-0.62) {Books borrowed in a week};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The dot plot shows the number of books each student borrowed in a week.
How many students borrowed exactly $1$ book?

options.why: Reads the value $1$ on the axis instead of counting the dots above it.
Counts the dots above $2$ instead of above $1$.
Gives the total number of students rather than how many borrowed $1$ book.

questions.solution_text:
Count the dots stacked above $1$
$=4\text{ students}$

questions.question_text:
The stem-and-leaf plot shows a set of scores.
$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\ \hline 3&2\;4\;4\\ 4&1\;7\\ 5&2\end{array}$
Key: $3\;|\;2$ means $32$.
What was the highest score?

options.why: Reads only the largest stem and ignores its leaf.
Gives the largest leaf digit instead of reading the whole score.
Chooses the score with the largest leaf digit, overlooking the larger stem $5$.

questions.solution_text:
Read the largest stem and its leaf: $5\;|\;2$
$=52$

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]\draw[{Stealth}-{Stealth}] (-0.6,0)--(5.6,0);\foreach \x in {0,1,2,3,4,5} {\draw (\x,0)--(\x,-0.12); \node[below] at (\x,-0.14) {$\x$};}\fill (0,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (0,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,1.26) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (3,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (3,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (5,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\node[below] at (2.5,-0.62) {Books borrowed in a week};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The dot plot shows the number of books $12$ students borrowed in a week.
How many students borrowed more than $2$ books?

options.why: Includes the $3$ students who borrowed exactly $2$ books; "more than $2$" excludes $2$.
Counts only the students who borrowed exactly $3$ books and omits the $5$-book reader.
Counts only the single student who borrowed $5$ books and omits the $3$-book readers.

questions.solution_text:
More than $2$ means $3$ or more books
$2\text{ students}+1\text{ student}$
$=3\text{ students}$
